questions.q: What two things does a single Microsoft Purview Data Map capacity unit (CU) measure together?
options: Number of users and number of reports
Operation throughput (ops/sec) and metadata storage (GB), bundled into one billable number
Scan duration and classification accuracy
Number of domains and number of collections
questions.explain: A capacity unit bundles operation throughput (25 ops/sec per CU) and metadata storage (10 GB per CU) together — you can't buy one without the other.

questions.q: By default, how far can a Data Map's capacity autoscale without requesting a quota increase?
options: It cannot autoscale at all
From 1 up to 10 capacity units
Unlimited, with no ceiling
From 1 up to 3 capacity units
questions.explain: A new account starts at 1 capacity unit and autoscales automatically up to 10 CUs based on load. Going beyond 10 requires a support quota increase request.

questions.q: How is Data Map billing calculated for a given hour?
options: By averaging throughput and storage usage across the entire month
Based on whichever of throughput or storage needs more capacity units that hour, with a 1 CU minimum
A flat fee regardless of usage
Only storage usage matters; throughput is never billed
questions.explain: Billing is hourly, and for each hour, Purview bills for the capacity units needed to cover whichever factor — throughput or storage — required more that hour, with a minimum of 1 CU.

questions.q: Where in the Azure portal can you watch your Purview account's Data Map Capacity Units and Storage Size in real time?
options: Only by contacting Microsoft support
The account's Overview page (Monitoring section) or Monitoring → Metrics for deeper analysis
These metrics are not available anywhere in the Azure portal
Only inside the Unified Catalog's glossary
questions.explain: The account Overview page's Monitoring section shows both metrics at a glance, and Monitoring → Metrics opens the full Azure Monitor experience for deeper analysis, including plotting scan outcome metrics alongside them.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of this lesson's practical levers for controlling Data Map capacity and cost?
options: Running incremental scans after the first full scan
Staggering scan schedules instead of running several at once
Disabling lineage extraction when it isn't needed
Permanently disabling all scanning for every data source
questions.explain: The practical levers are incremental scans, scoping scans, staggering schedules, reducing frequency, disabling unused lineage extraction, and cleaning up stale metadata — not disabling scanning entirely, which would defeat the Data Map's purpose.
